correctness.rationale: For every odd prime p, two quadratic pair-sums recover the residue multiset modulo p. Distinct residue classes lift uniquely in a fixed ordering because the pair-difference is a unit; equal classes reduce to convolution over F_p. Orthogonality, cyclic Parseval and (sum A)^2 expansion prove an exact decomposition with positive coefficients 2(p−2) and 1/p, so the entire complex equality set consists of one residue-character packet. A probability-of-largest-residue and Fourier-mass comparison proves the stated nonoptimal global distance bound. Standard-library replay verified 107 packet and arbitrary-input cases and four direct Fourier moments at p=3,5. Finite checks are consistency evidence only.

originality.rationale: The sharp p fourth-power constant is not novel in isolation: established maximum-fiber machinery plus standard packets gives it. The supported new claim is the exact two-component deficit, the classification of all complex extremizers as p² orthogonal residue-character rays and the consequent quantitative stability inequality. Full-text comparisons of the relevant general fiber bound, the same-ring packet theorem, sharp field extension, and finite-field moment-curve stability found no stated stronger implication that covers this combined claim. An older implicit equality-case argument remains a genuine residual risk.

value.rationale: The quadratic curve over the first nonfield residue ring is a canonical arithmetic Fourier-extension model. Identifying every optimizer, counting the p² orthogonal extremal rays and separating two distinct modes of failure of saturation yields more than a numerical sharp constant: it gives a structural rigidity theorem and a global near-extremizer distance estimate motivated by local-ring wave-packet theory. Higher prime powers and an optimal stability coefficient remain open outside the stated scope.
